links.comparator_used: AI support in interpretation only (no worklist prioritisation); secondarily current practice with no AI support
links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness (incremental cost per day reduction in time from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis or discharge from the lung cancer pathway)
links.effect: AI with prioritisation was not cost-effective vs AI without prioritisation; no AI was always more cost-effective. Budget impact was £2 million per year in England for AI with prioritisation vs AI without, rising to £16–35 million per year vs No AI. The underlying LungIMPACT trial found no reduction in time from CXR to lung cancer diagnosis.
links.tradeoff: Added cost to the NHS with no demonstrated reduction in time to diagnosis.
links.quote: AI with prioritisation was not cost-effective vs. AI without prioritisation and secondary analysis showed that no AI was always more cost-effective.

design_hint: AI-based worklist prioritisation of chest X-rays
